WEB-03a781657bb4.title: Funding Opportunities
WEB-03a781657bb4.summary: This page outlines multiple distinct funding opportunities from the Brain Canada Foundation rather than a single research funding call. Listed initiatives include the 2026 Future Leaders in Canadian Brain Research, the CanNRT-Brain Canada Fellowship, the 2026 Knowledge Mobilization Grants, and Innovation & Impact Grants. Each opportunity has separate objectives, funding levels, eligibility requirements, and deadlines for researchers, trainees, and clinician scientists studying brain health.

WEB-00773cbd93aa.title: Bridge Funding for Disrupted Neurodegenerative Research Grant Program (BFDN) Powering the Next Generation of Research
WEB-00773cbd93aa.programme: Bridge Funding for Disrupted Neurodegenerative Research (BFDN) grant program
WEB-00773cbd93aa.summary: This program supports early-career investigators whose research projects on Alzheimer's, Parkinson's, and related neurodegenerative disorders were disrupted by operational or priority changes in U.S. federal funding. Grants provide up to $250,000 for 3 to 12 months to cover salary and direct research costs, requiring up to 25% institutional cost-sharing. Eligible principal investigators must meet NIH Early Stage Investigator definitions (or be within seven years of designation) and have experienced specific disruptions to federal grants.
WEB-00773cbd93aa.eligible_countries: Not stated in the official text: check the call

GG-PAR-25-226.title: Seamless Early-Stage Clinical Drug Development (Phase 1 to 2a) for Novel therapeutic Agents for AD/ADRD
GG-PAR-25-226.programme_family: NIH – US National Institutes of Health
GG-PAR-25-226.summary: This funding opportunity supports the early-stage clinical drug development of novel, non-amyloid and non-tau therapeutic candidates for Alzheimer's disease and related dementias. It funds phased projects that bundle phase 1 clinical trials (UG3) with phase 1b/2a trials (UH3) to evaluate safety, dosing, pharmacokinetics, and target engagement. Applications are open to higher education institutions, nonprofits, for-profit businesses, and foreign non-U.S. organizations.
GG-PAR-25-226.countries_evidence: Non-domestic (non-U.S.) Entities (Foreign Organizations) are eligible to apply.
